notes:
Untested: this module has not been run in any configuration.

Departures from the plan:
1. CHK-033 preload: the plan loads all four INTR_CTRL_EN_* registers with 0x0F0F0F0F. That contradicts "no events" and INTR_STATE staying 0x100, because with both level-high and level-low enabled one level always holds. With i_gpio=0 the test loads LVLHIGH with 0x0F0F0F0F and sets LVLLOW to 0. A byte write wrongly accepted into LVLLOW would still show up as interrupts.
2. CHK-016: the second run (PutFullData to 0x14) happens in the same test, after a reset.
3. CHK-022 "opposite edge alone never sets": this can't be seen while the interrupt is latched. The test raises the configured edge, clears it with W1C while the input is held, then applies the opposite edge and expects INTR_STATE to read 0. The falling-edge case mirrors this.

Assumption to confirm:
- With GpioAsyncOn=0, all inputs including i_gpio change right after a falling edge, as the coding rules require. CHK-011(f) says inputs change only just after rising edges; if that assertion samples falling edges at the start of the time step, it will flag every input change in sync_off and min. With GpioAsyncOn=1, i_gpio changes at a random point in the clock period and E0 is computed from that point.

How it works:
- Timing: every edge number comes from samples taken at falling edges after all drives settle, recorded against the next rising edge.
- Host: the TL-UL host model gives each outstanding request its own a_source, holds the A channel until o_a_ready, can throttle d_ready randomly, and matches responses by d_source.
- Background checks: the host also watches CHK-012/013. A sampler watches CHK-001, 002, 005 and 008. Problems are collected and reported by env.finish() at the end of each test.
- Configurations: CHK-031 calls not_verifiable when GpioAsHwStrapsEn=0, and CHK-032 when it is 1.
- Regression: strap sampling (when on), then about 1200 random pipelined requests with stalls (sub-word reads, byte writes, bad requests, unmapped addresses, undefined opcodes) scored against the reference model in acceptance order, then an interrupt scoreboard against random edge/level settings, one ALERT_TEST alert, and one corrupted-integrity request followed by a reset.
